newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call money, term rates ease on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Manila call money, term rates ease on liquidity.

text.p: The Philippine call money and term rates eased on Wednesday due to high liquidity recently boosted by maturing Treasury bonds, traders said.
The average interbank call loan rate slipped to 18.03125 percent from Tuesday's 18.0625 percent. Turnover was light at 8.317 billion pesos with done deals ranging from 18.03125 to 18.25 percent.
About 2.6 billion pesos worth of three-year floating rate Treasury bonds matured earlier this week, flushing more funds into an already liquid market.
The secondary Treasury bills market was more active with aggressive bidders buying bills before rates go down further, she added.
T-bill rates went down slightly during its weekly auction Tuesday due to oversubscription.
More than 38 billion worths of bids were tendered in yesterday's bidding, but the auction committee accepted only 4.5 billion pesos worth of bids.
"You can imagine how many banks were scrambling for such a small volume of securities," another trader said.
